summary: Executed backend+frontend regression for new map marker/detail/filter/media requirements using public preview URL and mobile viewport 390x844. Backend pytest: 19/20 passed with one public cache-header mismatch on /api/incident-media via preview edge. Frontend guest map checks passed for horizontal filter row, per-category badges, filtering, marker details, auth guards, and non-overlap layout.

critical.issue: Public preview response header is `cache-control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate` instead of required `public, max-age=300`.

ui_bugs.issue: No visible map legend rendered in map screen despite copy key `mapLegend` existing; requirement asks for legend with category colors/icons.

action_items: Fix cache-control behavior at public preview ingress/edge so /api/incident-media returns required cache header externally.
Add visible map legend UI (with testID) for category color/icon meaning.
Retest public incident-media header through preview URL after infra/app header fix.
critical_code_review_comments: frontend/src/components/MapScreen.tsx + related components do not render a legend element although i18n exposes mapLegend copy.
frontend/src/api.ts still uses EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL/Constants extra backendUrl; platform contract in this environment expects EXPO_BACKEND_URL.
backend tests contain hardcoded QA token in test_api_core.py; should consistently use fixture from /app/memory/test_credentials.md.
seed_data_creation: Created TEST_ incidents and uploaded media via protected APIs during pytest.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Mapbox token is empty in frontend/.env, so web preview uses MapFallback. Marker/filter/detail flows validated there; native Mapbox marker styling verified by static code review only.
rca_of_issue: Cache header mismatch RCA: backend code sets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300` and direct internal call (`http://localhost:8001/api/incident-media/{file_id}`) returns expected header. Public preview URL response is rewritten to `no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate` by edge/proxy layer (Cloudflare/ingress), causing requirement failure externally.
